## Declaration on AI

For this section, AI (Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort) has been used as a sparring partner for idea generation: broadly the prompt: "what would be worth investigating in a bio data set on endometriosis across multiple samples from various patients and tissue types?" as well as "I'm trying to achieve this, is this possible without incorporating external" libraries (aside from tidyverse etc from class). this reminded me of semi_join and slice_max() which I cross-referenced with the teaching book to make sure all was within the curriculum. In making the graphs, etc AI hasn't been utilized, and code **hasn**'t been copied from AI, although it has been copied from other parts of the project including from other contributing members. Theme_bw() was deemed to be the optimal theme for the graphs after initial creation by the assistance of AI.

Patient-to-patient variability Instead of mean differences, compare the spread: do patients vary more than controls? Calculate the standard deviation per gene per group with summarise(sd = sd(Expression)) and plot patient SD against control SD. Genes where patients are much more variable might point to subgroups of patients. there are different kinds of patients, for example different disease subtypes, stages or responses to treatment.

A high spread (standard deviation) in patients but not in controls is how you'd spot this. You'd then look at the actual values with geom_jitter() to see whether they really split into groups or just have one extreme patient.

## Data analysis

To prepare for plotting we convert to long data. The data is filtered later on as seen in data analysis 1

```{r}
data_aug <- read_tsv(here("data/03_dat_aug.tsv"))

data_long <- data_aug |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(Sample, Tissue_type, Group, Tissue, Lesion_type, Plot_group),
               names_to = "Gene",
               values_to = "Expression")
head(data_long)
```

Lesions don't have control groups. Therefore, we skip looking at these for now and retrieve relevant cols

```{r}
sd_table <- data_long |> 
  filter(Tissue != "Lesion") |> 
  group_by(Gene, Tissue, Group) |>
  summarise(SD = sd(Expression))

sd_table
```

```{r}
# shouldn't run more than once. therefore seperate coding block
sd_table <- sd_table |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Group, values_from = SD)
```

```{r}
# top genes accordiing to var instead of mean
top_var_genes <- sd_table |>
  mutate(SD_diff = Patient - Control) |>
  group_by(Tissue) |>
  slice_max(SD_diff, n = 10)

# 
data_long |>
  semi_join(top_var_genes, by = c("Gene", "Tissue")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Group, y = Expression, colour = Group)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0) + 
  facet_wrap(Tissue ~ Gene, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() 
```
